note: Fits the physical and motivational profile precisely and fails on the money. Neglected_health is a match — nothing is in crisis, he is proactively getting ahead of ageing rather than repairing damage. Good_to_great is close to verbatim: "I'm relatively in good shape and muscular, but I want to keep it up and even improve", with the driver being 46-year-old muscle loss and a slowing metabolism rather than any problem. Not_deconditioned is a clear match — lifelong footballer still playing weekly, plus yoga and two gym sessions, describing himself as muscular; he is the opposite of the excluded profile. Income is a clear miss: he named $600 for six months as roughly his tolerance, is ending semi-private coaching specifically because it is expensive, and called $6,000 "a lot of money". Successful could not be assessed at all — occupation was established only as desk work in front of a computer with some travel, with no role, industry or ownership status ever asked or volunteered, so it is recorded in neither list. Recorded as edge rather than outside because the three criteria that were assessable all match cleanly and only one fails. Two observations for the rollup. First, the pattern across this batch is now consistent on five of five sales calls: every prospect who matched income closed or is live, and every prospect who missed it stalled or lost, regardless of how well they fit the rest of the definition. Second, this call is the clearest evidence in the batch that the range, not just the ICP, is the constraint — a well-qualified, well-motivated, in-profile prospect asked twice to buy something smaller and there was nothing to sell him.
